activities.caption: pair each courtroom term with its meaning
activities.name: ccTrackMatch

config.prompt: Each track has its own cast — pair the term with its meaning:

pairs.right: the Crown prosecutes (Rex or Regina) — even after the victim forgives
took charging decisions away from the police
does not "press charges" and cannot withdraw a prosecution
the claimant is master of the case — settling, abandoning or escalating at will

config.why: The deepest difference is purpose: a crime is a wrong against the community answered with blame; a civil wrong is a breach of duty answered with correction — restoring the injured party, so far as money can.

activities.anchor: because ordering someone to pay compensation is a survivable error
activities.caption: place the civil bar on the certainty scale
activities.name: ccProofPlace

config.prompt: The civil standard — "more likely than not" — sits just above what per cent?
config.why: The balance of probabilities (US: preponderance of the evidence) asks which story is more likely — a damages award is an error the system can absorb, while convicting the innocent is catastrophic: Blackstone's ratio (1769), better that ten guilty persons escape than that one innocent suffer.

activities.anchor: the case that makes the whole structure visible
activities.caption: bet on what the second jury could lawfully do
activities.name: ccSimpsonPredict

config.q: October 1995: a criminal jury acquits O.J. Simpson of two murders. February 1997: what can another jury lawfully do on the same evidence?
choices: Nothing — double jeopardy forbids any second look
Find him liable for the deaths and award $33.5 million to the families — a different jeopardy under a lower bar
Reopen the case only if the police admit an error
config.why: The criminal jury needed proof beyond reasonable doubt; the civil jury needed "more likely than not", saw the same evidence, and could lawfully reach the opposite bottom line — including $25 million punitive damages. The criminal bar is deliberately set where it is hard to clear.

activities.anchor: Both are needed because neither alone is fair
activities.caption: file each item under the liability element it belongs to
activities.name: ccElementsBuckets

config.prompt: The prosecutor must prove both — file each item:
buckets: no blame here — excuse or skip

items.label: a voluntary act (or culpable omission) causing the forbidden result
intention, recklessness or negligence as the offence demands
an unpredictable epileptic seizure behind the wheel
speeding under strict liability — enforcement impossible otherwise

config.why: Neither element alone is fair — and defences each mark a moment when society forfeits its right to blame.

activities.caption: line up negligence in logical order
activities.name: ccNegligenceOrder

config.prompt: Negligence has four elements — order them as the claim must build:
items: a breach of the standard of the reasonable person
config.why: The polarity shift tells the tracks apart: criminal law asks "what kind of person are you?" (blame); civil law asks "who should bear this loss?" (allocation) — which is why contributory negligence splits the loss in civil law but carelessness is no defence to assault.

activities.caption: call the magistrates' share of criminal work
activities.name: ccMagistratesEstimate

config.prompt: What share of criminal cases in England and Wales do magistrates' courts handle?
config.why: Roughly 95 per cent — summary offences entirely, either-way offences unless sent up; the magistrates are unpaid Justices of the Peace advised on law by a legal adviser, a medieval institution still doing the bulk of the work. Civil claims are the mirror image: well under 5 per cent of issued claims ever reach trial — settlement is the system's normal output.

activities.anchor: conviction is public condemnation in the community's name
activities.caption: drag the divider — cement versus harm
activities.name: ccDevlinCompare

config.prompt: May the state criminalise private conduct most citizens find immoral? Drag between the answers:

before.label: Devlin: morality as cement
before.text: Shared morality is the "cement" of society — attacks on it threaten the fabric itself, so the state may criminalise.

after.label: Hart: harm as the limit
after.text: Harm to others is the proper limit; morality enforced by law is neither free nor truly moral — and in practice consensual private conduct has been steadily decriminalised since Wolfenden (1957).

config.why: The debate keeps returning with each new question — drug use, assisted dying, online speech: society deciding whether it answers with condemnation or leaves the matter to private adjustment.

activities.anchor: and an acquitted person must be able to live
activities.caption: pair each double-jeopardy boundary with its case
activities.name: ccJeopardyMatch

config.prompt: Finality and its two boundaries — pair each with its instance:

pairs.right: the bar on trying someone twice for the same offence — the state has had its full attempt
a civil claim is a different jeopardy entirely (the Simpson lesson)
the Criminal Justice Act 2003: an acquittal can be quashed where new and compelling evidence emerges and the DPP consents
the 2012 conviction of Gary Dobson and David Norris for the racist murder of Stephen Lawrence (1993), after new forensic evidence

config.why: A change justified as fixing one injustice without reopening the floodgates — though critics still argue finality is worth its price.
